sections.title: Premise
sections.why: The premise is the shortest true statement of your game’s story, and every other entry in the bible has to agree with it.

seed.label: Seed
seed.guide: One sentence, under 15 words, with no character names.
questions: Who has the most to lose? Describe them without using a name.
What do they want to win, or keep from losing?
Who is the player in this story, and what do they get to do?
Put those together in one sentence of fewer than 15 words.

sketch.label: Sketch
sketch.guide: One paragraph of about five sentences: the setup, what changes, what follows, the turn, and the ending.
questions: Setup: who, where, and what’s normal before anything changes?
What changes, and why can’t they go back to the way things were?
What happens because of that? What do they try, and what does it lead to?
What turn, choice, or discovery pushes them toward the end?
How does it end, and what’s different for them afterward?

sheet.label: Sheet
sheet.guide: About a page. Give each sentence of your Sketch its own paragraph.
questions: Who are they, where are they, and what does an ordinary day look like?
What changes their world, and what does it ask of them?
What follows from that, one thing leading to the next?
What turn changes how they see their situation, and what do they do about it?
How does it end, what does it cost, and what stays changed?

seed.label: Seed
seed.guide: One sentence: who they are and the shape of their story.
questions: Who is this person, and what’s the shape of their story? Say it in one sentence.

sketch.label: Sketch
sketch.guide: One paragraph: their story from start to finish, as they live it.
questions: Tell their story in a paragraph: where they start, what changes, and where they end up.

sheet.label: Sheet
sheet.guide: As much as you know. Leave anything you haven’t decided.

fields.label: Name
fields.question: What’s their full name, and what do other people call them? Who uses which name?

fields.label: Type
fields.question: What kind of being are they, and where do they belong?

fields.label: Archetype
fields.question: Which patterns do they fit? Pick any that apply, or name your own.

fields.label: Age
fields.question: How old are they? If age doesn’t apply, or it’s complicated, say how.

fields.label: Gender identity or expression
fields.question: How do they understand and express their gender?

fields.label: Physical appearance
fields.question: What would someone notice first, and what only later? Include distinguishing marks: skin, birthmarks, scars, tattoos.

fields.label: Voice
fields.question: What do they sound like? How fast, how loud, and which words do they reach for?

fields.label: Personality
fields.question: What are they like to be around, and where do they contradict themselves?

fields.label: Background and history
fields.question: Where do they come from, and what happened that still shapes them?

fields.label: Want and need
fields.question: What do they want, and what do they actually need?

fields.label: The lie they believe
fields.question: What do they believe about themselves or the world that isn’t true?

fields.label: What stands in their way
fields.question: What’s against them, outside and inside?

fields.label: Arc
fields.question: How are they different at the end, or why do they stay the same?

fields.label: Relevance to the story
fields.question: Why does the story need them?

fields.label: Playable or NPC
fields.question: Can the player be this character, or do they meet them?

fields.label: Gameplay role
fields.question: What do they do in play: guide, rival, vendor, boss, companion?

fields.label: Barks and callouts
fields.question: What do they say in passing, in combat, or when the player lingers?

fields.label: Secrets
fields.question: What are they hiding, and from whom?

fields.label: Relationships
fields.question: Who matters most to them, and how?

fields.label: Appearances
fields.question: Where do they appear in the story?
